A description tells a reader what something is like; a procedure tells them how to decide. Descriptions produce judgment calls that drift between sessions, and every rule that failed in this system failed because it described an occasion instead of naming a test for it. FOUR TRIGGERS, all detectable. (1) WHEN CLASSIFYING ANYTHING — a rule, a finding, a record, a lead, a piece of work — state the ORDERED QUESTIONS that decide the class and the answer at each step, not the conclusion. A classification without its questions cannot be checked or repeated. (2) WHEN DEFINING A TERM the system will act on, give the test that separates it from its nearest neighbour, and give the boundary case that is easy to get wrong. If a definition admits no failing example it is not a definition. (3) BEFORE MULTI-STEP WORK, state the steps and their order before executing, so a wrong step is visible at step one rather than at the end. (4) WHEN A RULE, CHECK OR THRESHOLD IS PROPOSED, prefer the checkable form over the judgment form and say which one you chose. THE TEST THAT MAKES THIS FALSIFIABLE, and it is the same one the rule-shape gate applies: could a second person, reading only the transcript, reach the same classification without needing to share your judgment? If not, the procedure is still a description. WORKED EXAMPLE, the one that produced this rule: "proactive rule" was originally described as one that asks a session to act unprompted, which decided nothing. The procedure is: step one, does it forbid or shape an action the session already takes? then it is a constraint or a transform and it self-fires. Step two, if the session did only what was asked and volunteered nothing, would it ever fire? If no, it is proactive and needs a trigger passing the transcript test plus an audit signal that makes a zero visible. Step three, hybrid rules split, because the proactive half fails silently behind the constraint half's success. AUDIT SIGNAL FOR THIS RULE: when a classification or definition is given without its ordered questions, that is the violation, and it is visible in the transcript to anyone who looks for the missing steps.

CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session is about to say anything about UNCOMMITTED WORK, a DIRTY TREE, or who is BLOCKING whom: measure against `origin/<branch>`, never against HEAD, and check the SIGN of the diff before naming an owner.

    git fetch -q origin && git diff origin/main --stat [-- <paths>]

WHY HEAD IS THE WRONG BASE. On a shared checkout, local main drifts behind origin constantly — several sessions push, one tree lags. `git diff --stat` against a base that is N commits behind reports every line those N commits added as though it were somebody's uncommitted work. On 2026-08-14 that produced "238 insertions across five files, blocking every other session", named a specific session as the owner, and issued that session a relocation instruction under internal-procedure authority. All five files were already on origin; the diff was empty against it. The session named held nothing and was never the blocker. A peer refuted it in one command. The ahead/behind count (8 ahead, 5 behind) had been printed in that same session earlier and was used as the comparison base anyway.

READ THE SIGN, which is the second half and the cheaper tell. A working copy showing NET NEGATIVE against origin — fewer lines than the repo has — cannot be anyone's uncommitted work. It is a STALE CHECKOUT: the disk is behind the repo. That distinction decides everything downstream, because in-flight work must be waited for and left alone, while a stale tree must be brought forward and is nobody's property to protect. Calling the second the first stalls everyone indefinitely waiting on work that does not exist.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A WRONG SENTENCE. ops/githooks/pre-push runs ops/ci.sh against the DISK, so a stale tree means the next push tests code the repo already replaced and reports green on it. A merged fix that never reached disk is how the git-hook fixture hijack fired twice on 2026-08-13.

COMPOSES WITH the rule that an uncommitted file belongs to the session that wrote it and no other party resolves it. That rule is correct and unchanged — this one is upstream of it, because you cannot apply an ownership rule until you have established the thing is actually uncommitted.

A CHECK MUST COMPARE THE ARTIFACT AGAINST WHAT IT SHOULD BE, AND A SUCCESS SIGNAL MUST BE DERIVED FROM READING THAT ARTIFACT. Binds at two named moments.

MOMENT 1 — BUILDING OR REVIEWING ANY GUARD. The test is never "is it non-empty" and never "did the command exit 0". Ask what the artifact looks like when it is RIGHT, and compare against that: a floor derived from the last known-good instance, a structural marker the producer writes only on success, a count. On 2026-08-07 bin/backup-dump.sh guarded the nightly backup with `[ -s "$OUT.tmp" ]` — more than zero bytes. pg_dump lost its Neon connection mid-dump, age encrypted the empty stream into a 200-byte file, the guard passed it, `mv` promoted it to that day's official backup, the archiver uploaded it to R2 as the durable off-Mac copy, and the dead-man switch was pinged. MOMENT 2 — WIRING ANY SIGNAL THAT REPORTS ON WORK. A signal that reports on work it did not read is a FALSE signal and gets rewired or removed, never left in place. Three instruments agreed the backup succeeded that night and not one had read it: the healthchecks dead-man ping fired because the chain reached the end rather than because the backup was good; `set -eu` without `set -o pipefail` returned age's exit status instead of pg_dump's, so the failing stage was invisible; and the success line printed `du -h`, which floors at the [synthetic_money_shorthand_1] block size and therefore physically could not display 200 bytes as wrong. A hang is the same defect at the limit — the R2 archiver blocked for 3h20m on an untimed DB read, so the chain never returned, `set -e` never fired, and the scheduled task reported nothing at all. An exit-code check can never catch that, because there is no exit code.

If no line reads it, the check is decoration and must be treated as an outstanding defect, not a passing check. CONSTRAINT, binding at the moment a session is about to say it HANDED OFF, SENT, DELIVERED, NOTIFIED or PASSED something on: name the recipient, or do not use the word. Writing a record is not delivering it. A decision entry, a loop row, a finding and a doctrine section are all durable and findable, and none of those properties makes anything reach anyone. The verbs that RECORD are a different set from the verbs that DELIVER, and using the first while claiming the second is the failure this closes.

THE TEST, one question: WHO OR WHAT RECEIVED IT? If the answer is "a future session will find it", that is a record, not a handoff — say "written to the record" and say where. If a handoff is genuinely wanted, deliver it: `list_sessions` shows the user's other sessions with their titles and whether they are running, and `send_message` puts the text into one as a user turn labelled with this session's title. Both exist and neither needs the partner.

THE AUDIT SIGNAL: before claiming a handoff, the target must have been NAMED — a session id, a person, an address. A sentence that reports a handoff with no recipient in it is the defect, and it is visible in the sentence itself.

WHAT IT COST, 2026-08-10. At the end of an overnight loop sweep, with context nearly exhausted, a session wrote a decision-history entry titled "HANDOFF — Loop Cleanup Continuation" and reported to synthetic_operator that it had handed off. Nothing had received it. synthetic_operator asked "what session did you hand off to?" — and the session then discovered that "Loop cleanup continuation" ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS RUNNING, created by synthetic_operator, one `list_sessions` call away the entire time. The briefing would have sat in a file while the live session it was written for carried on without it, and the failure would have been invisible, because a written record looks identical whether or not anyone read it.

THIS EXTENDS d8c9b1f0 — a finding that only exists in a record has not reached the partner — from findings to handoffs and to every other claim of delivery. Same principle, and the same reason it keeps mattering: durability and delivery are different properties, and only one of them is what the word claims.

A merged row is still a row. `find` reported 17 duplicate [synthetic_person_name_1] orgs when 1 was live; an auditor's "42 excess duplicate persons" was marked stale at 57 by a reviewer counting tombstones, then found exactly right at 42; a session reported 308 floating parties when 306 were the org layer doing its job and the real orphan count was 2. Before calling a record or a prior claim wrong, check `schema_migrations.applied_at` and `git log` for something that changed AFTER it was written. A verdict that blames an author for a defect we then repaired is worse than no verdict, because it teaches the next reader to discount a report that was right. Every single one was found by RE-RUNNING THE QUERY. def as_list(value):
    if value is None:
        return []
    parts = value.split(",") if isinstance(value, str) else list(value)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if str(p).strip()]


def build_url(payload):
    to = as_list(payload.get("to"))
    if not to:
        raise SystemExit("refusing to create a draft with no recipient")
    q = urllib.parse.quote          # %20 for spaces — see note 2 above
    parts = [f"subject={q(payload.get('subject') or '')}",
             f"body={q(payload.get('body') or '')}"]
    if as_list(payload.get("cc")):
        parts.append("cc=" + q(",".join(as_list(payload["cc"]))))
    if as_list(payload.get("bcc")):
        parts.append("bcc=" + q(",".join(as_list(payload["bcc"]))))
    return "mailto:" + q(",".join(to), safe="@,") + "?" + "&".join(parts)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Create a real Outlook draft. Never sends.")
    ap.add_argument("--to")
    ap.add_argument("--cc")
    ap.add_argument("--bcc")
    ap.add_argument("--subject")
    ap.add_argument("--body")
    ap.add_argument("--leave-open", action="store_true",
                    help="leave the compose window on screen instead of closing it")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.to or args.subject or args.body:
        payload = {k: v for k, v in vars(args).items() if v is not None}
    else:
        raw = sys.stdin.read().strip()
        if not raw:
            raise SystemExit("no input: pass flags or pipe JSON on stdin")
        payload = json.loads(raw)

    url = build_url(payload)
    if len(url) > 1900:
        # mailto has a practical length ceiling and a silently TRUNCATED draft is
        # far worse than a refusal: it looks finished and is not.
        raise SystemExit(
            f"body too long for the mailto route ({len(url)} chars of URL). "
            f"A truncated draft would look complete and would not be. Shorten it, "
            f"or use bin/gmail-handover.py for long text.")

    subprocess.run(["open", "-a", "Microsoft Outlook", url], check=False)

    mode = "leave" if args.leave_open else "close"

    out = (r.stdout or r.stderr).strip()
    if not out.startswith("OK"):
        raise SystemExit(f"draft may not have been saved: {out}")
    print(f"draft saved to Drafts: {payload.get('subject')!r}"
